newsitem.title: POLAND: Philips opens Polish television production unit.
newsitem.headline: Philips opens Polish television production unit.

text.p: Philips Electronics on Thursday opened a new production unit at its northern Polish television factory in Kwidzyn, which it sees as a stepping stone in its Polish expansion.
"This official celebration is a real milestone since 1921 when Philips came to Poland," Polish division head Jaap van Oost said during a celebration marking the opening of the unit.
Philips has been present since July 1995 at the Kwidzyn factory, which employs 1,100 and also produces video and compact disc players.
The factory is owned by Philips Consumer Electronics Industries sp zoo, where Philips holds 85 percent and Poland's Brabork electronics plant 15 percent.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, also present, said Philips' presence was an example of cooperation that Poland needed: investment providing jobs and paving Poland's way to international markets.
"The Polish economy has to develop while being open to the world and being open to foreign investment....I'm sure Philips has not its last word in Poland," Kwasniewski said.
The Kwidzyn factory wants to produce 5.5 million tuners and 350,000 televisions this year and 5.6 million tuners and one million televisions next year.
Dutch Philips Electronics has invested $200 million in Poland since it returned in 1991 after the post-war nationalisation of its factories.
It has majority stakes in nine companies here.
Jan Tollenaar, Philips Electronics deputy president, said most of Philips' activity in Eastern Europe was in Poland.
He said Philips' sales in the region were currently at one billion guilder a year, up from 250 million five years ago, with turnover in Poland at $300-350 million a year.
"In Poland we are experiencing tremendous growth...if there is a company which has linked its fate with Poland it's Philips," he said.
He also said Philips had investment plans in other Eastern Europe countries but they were lower than those for Poland.
Van Oost said Philips was looking for partners and possibilities for further investment in Poland, but said it was against his company policy to discuss such plans in detail.
"We are in the process of investigating further opportunities," he said.
